subject.title: [Feature]: Per-binding and per-agent permissionMode for ACP sessions

question: Should scoped ACP permission defaults be exposed as a generic permissionProfile contract on bindings[].acp and agents.list[].runtime.acp, or as ACPX-specific permissionMode and nonInteractivePermissions keys?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the public config shape controls write and shell authority for non-interactive ACP sessions and could either align with generic ACP runtime options or create an ACPX-specific parallel surface.

options.title: Use generic permissionProfile defaults
options.body: Add scoped permissionProfile defaults that map through the existing ACP runtime option layer, keeping ACPX-specific permissionMode names at the plugin-global layer.

options.title: Add ACPX-specific scoped keys
options.body: Implement the requested permissionMode and optional nonInteractivePermissions precedence directly for ACPX sessions, accepting a backend-specific public config surface.

options.title: Keep global config only
options.body: Document global ACPX config and live ACP runtime controls as the supported paths and leave static scoped permission defaults out for now.

recommendation.title: Use generic permissionProfile defaults
recommendation.body: Add scoped permissionProfile defaults that map through the existing ACP runtime option layer, keeping ACPX-specific permissionMode names at the plugin-global layer.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns both the ACP runtime option shape and the ACPX runtime integration most likely to define the durable permission contract.
